title: The Core Facilitator must justify ordinary decisions using only publicly available information
content:
A.1.7.7 imposes an unusually strong transparency constraint: "The Core Facilitator must ensure that their decisions related to ordinary operations are clearly explained and justified using publicly available information. The Core Facilitator is generally prohibited from basing their decisions on internal knowledge or undisclosed data that is not accessible to the public."

The prohibition is on the **input**, not just the explanation. A rule requiring decisions to be explained publicly is satisfied by a good write-up of a decision actually made on private grounds. A rule forbidding reliance on private information means the reasoning must be reconstructible from scratch by anyone — which is a far stronger property, and the only one that lets the community actually audit a facilitator rather than merely read them.

The annotations mark the boundaries carefully. "Internal knowledge" (A.1.7.7.0.3.1) covers "messages in private chats, internal memos, emails, or proprietary data" — exactly the material a well-connected facilitator would naturally accumulate and naturally rely on. "Publicly available information" (A.1.7.7.0.3.3) means accessible "without any special access rights or permissions." "Ordinary operations" (A.1.7.7.0.3.2) scopes the rule to routine day-to-day matters and "excludes decisions involving extraordinary circumstances and emergencies."

The exception is narrow and comes with a preference, mirroring A.1.5.9.3.0.4.1's treatment of adjudication reports: limited exceptions apply for sensitive security matters, but "even in these situations, the Core Facilitator should ensure that the rationale for their decision is communicated in a manner that respects security concerns while maintaining as much transparency as possible."

What this rule protects against is capture by information asymmetry. A facilitator who may act on private knowledge is unchallengeable — every objection can be met with "you don't know what I know" — and that is precisely the position from which a captured actor operates indistinguishably from an honest one.
description: A.1.7.7 generally prohibits basing decisions on internal knowledge or undisclosed data, making routine facilitator reasoning reproducible by any community member from public sources.
